question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Lineage barcoding with pre-treatment sister-cell tracking
ideas.description: Label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and compare which barcodes survive in replicate arms. Recurrence of the same clones across replicates indicates pre-existing, heritable states, while random survivors indicate stochastic or non-heritable states.

ideas.title: Single-cell multi-omics of persisters over time
ideas.description: Run scRNA-seq paired with scATAC-seq on cells before treatment, during drug exposure, and after regrowth, to identify transcriptional and chromatin states enriched in survivors. Trajectory and RNA-velocity analysis can show whether persisters arise from a rare pre-existing state or are induced by the drug.

ideas.title: Live-cell imaging with reporters and retrospective fate mapping
ideas.description: Image single cells for days before and after drug addition using fluorescent reporters of signaling (such as ERK or AKT activity), cell cycle, and stress. Then link each cell's pre-treatment history, such as signaling dynamics, cell-cycle phase, or mitochondrial content, to its survival outcome, and isolate survivors for sequencing.

ideas.title: Pooled CRISPR screens plus pharmacologic perturbation of candidate states
ideas.description: Run genome-wide or epigenetic-focused CRISPR knockout/interference screens under drug to find genes that raise or lower persister frequency. Then validate causal mechanisms, such as drug efflux, anti-apoptotic buffering, or oxidative stress (e.g., GPX4/ferroptosis), with targeted inhibitors.

ideas.title: Quantitative modeling of switching rates (fluctuation tests)
ideas.description: Use Luria-Delbrück-style fluctuation assays and sorted subpopulations to measure the rates at which cells switch into and out of the drug-tolerant state, and its memory duration. Fit stochastic models to the data to distinguish genetic mutation, epigenetic switching, and drug-induced adaptation, and predict dosing schedules that minimize persisters.
